title: Arrest Turns Physical as Suspect Resists Officers' Commands
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Picayune, Mississippi — On December 15, 2024, Picayune Police Officers were dispatched to a business on Jackson Landing Road in reference to Randall “Randy” Perkins making inappropriate comments toward employees and telling one he knew which car was hers and that he “had something for her and was coming back”. He also used his fingers to shape a gun and told another employee “I have you bi**h”. Perkins advanced toward one of the employees and it took a customer intervening so he couldn’t contact her. The police department was called and he left prior to officers arriving. Perkins returned on December 19, 2024, causing a disturbance, cursing at employees and telling them “I got you”. He again left before police arrived. On December 24, 2024, the employees notified police that Perkins had returned. 

As an officer approached, he observed Perkins near the front landing of the business and contacted Perkins a short distance away as he was walking away. Perkins initially denied being there however the responding officer saw him. The responding officer told Perkins four times to place his hands on the bumper of his vehicle. As the officer grabbed Perkins right hand he turned away from him and the officer took Perkins to the ground in an attempt to place him into custody. Perkins is told repeatedly to give the officer his hands and lay on his belly. The officer continued to tell Perkins to give him his hands but he tucked them underneath himself and attempted to push up. Perkins also tucked his legs underneath himself in an attempt to get up and the officer had to push Perkins down at the base of the back of his neck. The officer delivered 8-10 short punches to Perkins right side and two knee strikes to the same area without success. 

Additional officers arrived and one officer drive stunned the middle of Perkins back which did not appear to be successful. A drive stun is a technique used with the taser where contact is made at close distance rather than deploying a cartridge. Although the taser was in contact with Perkins, it was only deployed for one – five second cycle. It took the additional officers to restrain Perkins and place him into custody. He was then transported to the Lenoir Rowell Criminal Justice Center where he was booked and incarcerated for Trespassing, Disorderly Conduct and Resisting Arrest. He also has pending charges from the incidents where he threatened and acted disorderly with employees from the business. The officer’s response to Perkins resistance is being investigated. Perkins has been trespassed from multiple businesses in town and has been arrested multiple times for doing so.
